module_name: Education Access E-Learning Academy — Form One Mathematics
title: Form One Mathematics Mastery Framework
purpose: To establish clear, measurable criteria for evaluating learners' mathematical understanding, procedural fluency, reasoning, application, communication, and independent learning.

mastery_domains.name: Conceptual Understanding
mastery_domains.description: Understanding mathematical concepts, relationships, principles, definitions, and representations.

mastery_domains.name: Procedural Fluency
mastery_domains.description: Applying mathematical procedures accurately, efficiently, and appropriately.

mastery_domains.name: Mathematical Reasoning
mastery_domains.description: Using logical thinking, mathematical arguments, and evidence to justify solutions.
indicators: Identifies relevant information in a problem.
Explains the choice of a mathematical method.
Recognises and corrects errors in reasoning.

mastery_domains.name: Mathematical Application
mastery_domains.description: Applying mathematical knowledge to everyday situations and unfamiliar problems.
indicators: Recognises mathematical ideas in practical situations.
Translates real situations into mathematical expressions.
Interprets answers in their original context.

mastery_domains.name: Mathematical Communication
mastery_domains.description: Communicating mathematical thinking clearly using appropriate language, symbols, diagrams, and representations.
indicators: Presents mathematical work in an organised manner.
Communicates mathematical ideas verbally and in writing.

mastery_domains.name: Independent Learning and Reflection
mastery_domains.description: Demonstrating responsibility, persistence, academic integrity, and reflective learning.

mastery_levels.name: Beginning
mastery_levels.description: The learner demonstrates initial awareness but requires substantial guidance.
mastery_levels.progression_requirement: Recognises basic concepts and attempts introductory activities.

mastery_levels.name: Developing
mastery_levels.description: The learner demonstrates partial understanding and can complete familiar tasks with some support.
mastery_levels.progression_requirement: Explains basic concepts and completes routine exercises with improving accuracy.

mastery_levels.name: Proficient
mastery_levels.description: The learner demonstrates secure understanding and independently completes expected Form One tasks.
mastery_levels.progression_requirement: Applies procedures accurately, explains reasoning, and solves familiar practical problems.

mastery_levels.name: Advanced
mastery_levels.description: The learner demonstrates strong mathematical understanding and applies knowledge flexibly to unfamiliar situations.
mastery_levels.progression_requirement: Solves complex problems, justifies strategies, and communicates mathematical reasoning independently.

assessment_evidence.discover: Initial responses demonstrating prior knowledge and conceptual awareness.
assessment_evidence.learn: Accurate notes, definitions, explanations, and interpretation of examples.
assessment_evidence.knowledge_check: Independent responses demonstrating understanding of key concepts.
assessment_evidence.apply: Solutions to practical and unfamiliar mathematical problems.
assessment_evidence.journal: Reflections identifying achievements, challenges, and improvement strategies.
assessment_evidence.friday_assessment: Weekly assessment results and evidence of corrected errors.
assessment_evidence.evidence_and_mastery: Organised portfolio demonstrating achievement across mastery domains.

progression_rules.principle: Progression must be based on demonstrated competence rather than activity completion alone.
requirements: Review evidence across all relevant mastery domains.
Identify concepts or skills requiring further development.
Provide corrective teaching and additional practice where necessary.
progression_rules.teacher_authority: The teacher or authorised learning facilitator validates mastery decisions using assessment evidence and professional judgement.

feedback_principles: Provide specific feedback linked to learning objectives.
Identify both strengths and areas requiring improvement.
intervention_steps: Determine the underlying misconception or difficulty.
Provide an appropriate explanation or worked example.

quality_assurance.assessment_alignment: Assessment activities must correspond to the intended learning objectives and mathematical competencies.
quality_assurance.fairness: Assessment criteria must be clear, consistent, and appropriate to the learner's level.
quality_assurance.authenticity: Evidence must represent the learner's own mathematical understanding and performance.
quality_assurance.record_integrity: Mastery decisions must be supported by documented assessment evidence.
quality_assurance.curriculum_alignment: Implementation must remain aligned with the applicable Tanzania Institute of Education Form One Mathematics curriculum.

completion_message: Mathematical mastery is demonstrated through understanding, accuracy, reasoning, application, communication, and the ability to work independently.
